description: The response header set of SB3 in standards/085-security-baseline.md, as data. Three response classes: document (anything a browser renders as a page), api (a representation a program consumes: JSON, problem+json, an event stream), asset (a static file the document loads). For each class, each required header and how its value is judged: 'exact' compares the whole value case-insensitively; 'one-of' admits any listed value; 'hsts', 'csp-document', 'csp-api', 'permissions-policy', 'no-store', 'no-store-unless-declared-public' and 'immutable' are directive checks whose meaning is stated on the entry. 'forbidden' headers are a finding when present in any class; 'constrained' headers are a finding when their value breaks the stated constraint; the 'superseded' header is never a finding and never satisfies the header that superseded it. Findings are the slugs named on each entry; contracts/security-baseline/corpus.json 'headers' is judged by applying this file.

document.is: A response a browser renders as a page: the web client's shell, a server-rendered view, an error page.

strict-transport-security.preload: admitted, never required; sent only on a registrable domain its owner has submitted to the preload list
strict-transport-security.why: A browser that has seen it never sends the first request in clear again; includeSubDomains because a cookie set on the apex reaches every subdomain and one unprotected subdomain is a cookie in clear.

content-security-policy.canonical: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-<nonce>' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'

directives.frame-ancestors: present; 'none' unless the origins allowed to frame are named

content-security-policy.report_only: Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only is admitted during a rollout and does not satisfy the rule
content-security-policy.why: Scripts run only when carrying this response's nonce and scripts they load are trusted transitively, so an injected script runs nowhere. No 'unsafe-inline', no 'unsafe-eval', no host or scheme allow-list in script-src.

x-content-type-options.why: Content sniffing turns a user upload served as text into a script.

referrer-policy.why: A document's URL may carry an id; a cross-origin navigation gets the origin only.

permissions-policy.why: Features the product does not use are denied to every frame, the product's own included; a product that uses one names it (self) with a Conventions entry.

cross-origin-opener-policy.why: Severs the window reference a cross-origin opener would otherwise hold.

cross-origin-resource-policy.why: A response may be embedded only by the origin, or site, that owns it.

cache-control.why: A nonced document is uncacheable by construction: a cached copy carries a nonce the next response's policy does not accept.

api.is: A representation a program consumes: JSON, problem+json, an event stream. A browser navigated to its URL renders it, so it is made inert.

strict-transport-security.why: HSTS is a property of the host, and the first response a browser sees from it may be any class.

content-security-policy.why: Nothing may load, nothing may frame it, and sandbox makes it inert if rendered.

x-content-type-options.why: A JSON body is never to be sniffed into HTML.

referrer-policy.why: An API URL is never a referrer anyone needs.

cross-origin-resource-policy.why: same-site under 060 AU7's topology B, where the API is a subdomain of the document's site.

cache-control.why: An authenticated response is one person's data and never enters a shared cache; an endpoint the OpenAPI document declares public and cacheable states its own policy, and the header must still be present.

asset.is: A static file the document loads: a hashed bundle chunk, a font, an image. Cacheable forever only because its name is its content hash.

strict-transport-security.why: HSTS is a property of the host.

x-content-type-options.why: A font or an image served with the wrong type must not become a script.

cross-origin-resource-policy.why: An asset is embedded by its own document.

cache-control.why: The name is the content hash, so the bytes at that name never change; an asset without a hashed name is not this class and gets no-cache.

x-xss-protection.why: Every browser has removed the auditor it controlled, and '1; mode=block' introduced information leaks of its own.

server.why: Where the edge insists on a Server header it carries a product token and never a version.

x-frame-options.why: Browsers consult frame-ancestors first and ignore X-Frame-Options when it is present. Sending DENY beside frame-ancestors 'none' is harmless duplication; a response carrying X-Frame-Options and no frame-ancestors has relied on the header consulted second.

nonce.why: Minted for this response from a cryptographic source and never reused; every <script> the document carries bears it.

asserted_by.api_class: the /readyz response of the started image
asserted_by.document_class: the / response of a started image that serves documents
asserted_by.delegated_to_edge: a header set by the edge is declared in the repository's Conventions and asserted by a live check against the deployed environment
